answer: Peers cross-check work history against a shared meadow of attested records, and any unexplained delta between claimed and observed output triggers slashing of the stake. Each agent must stake a bonded credential whose reputation grows along a single vine of verified contributions; creating a new identity resets it to zero, so splitting into many sybils forfeits accumulated trust. An attacker must therefore fund and sustain many costly stakes while gaining nothing, making large-scale sock-puppet farming economically irrational. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
